findings.finding: Final SSIM is essentially flat over 0-30% uplink packet loss for all four F-SIBS variants (30-trial means; max observed change -0.0004).
findings.evidence: stat_packet_loss.csv (recorded): per-cell std 0.0018-0.0033 dwarfs the mean trend
findings.interpretation: Federated dictionary construction degrades gracefully under uplink loss on this scene.
findings.limitation: Single scene (dino); loss applied to basis transmissions only; no retransmission model.

findings.finding: At every loss rate of the sweep the F-SIBS variants exceed NDIC-real by ~0.19 SSIM and LDMIC-equiv by ~0.15 SSIM (single-run).
findings.metric: final SSIM by method x rate
findings.interpretation: Under the adapted loss model, federated basis sharing retains a large quality advantage over the distributed baselines.
findings.limitation: Baselines evaluated under the same adapted loss model, not their native protocols; single run.

findings.finding: Global dictionary coherence remains 0.9127-0.9634 under 0-20% loss (F-SIBS variants, single-run).
findings.interpretation: Dropped transmissions do not destabilise the learned dictionary in the recorded runs.
findings.limitation: Coherence of baselines undefined (NaN by design).

findings.finding: Single-run sweep shows non-monotonic SSIM steps (e.g. F-SIBS_3: 0.7503 at 20% vs 0.7463 at 0% loss).
findings.interpretation: Consistent with stochastic dropout-draw noise; flagged rather than smoothed.
findings.limitation: n=1 sweep; multi-trial grid uses coarser rates {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3}.
